name: data-analysis
raw_brief_text: For an applied statistics course, analyze a provided CSV of monthly rainfall measurements from four weather stations. Produce a reproducible Python analysis that parses station, month, and millimeter values; reports per-station observation count, mean, median, and sample standard deviation; identifies the wettest station-month; and creates one comparison chart. Validate missing and nonnumeric values, include a fixed-fixture test, and write a short methods section explaining the use of sample standard deviation and any data exclusions. Do not fetch data from the internet.
rubric_text: 1. Automated: Per-station summaries and wettest station-month match independently computed fixture values. 2. Automated: Missing and nonnumeric measurements are reported as invalid rows. 3. Human judgment: The methods section explains statistical choices and data limitations accurately.

project_spec.title: Reproducible Multi-Station Rainfall Analysis
project_spec.description: Create a reproducible Python analysis of a local CSV containing monthly rainfall measurements from four stations. Validate station, month, and millimeter values; compute the specified per-station summaries and wettest station-month; produce a comparison chart, fixture-based tests, and a methods section describing statistical choices and exclusions.
deliverables: A Python analysis that reads a local rainfall CSV and validates required fields and numeric values.
Per-station observation count, mean, median, and sample standard deviation, plus the wettest station-month.
A comparison chart, automated fixed-fixture tests, and a methods section.
constraints: The input is a local CSV with station, month, and millimeter columns.
Missing or nonnumeric measurement values must be reported as invalid rows.
The analysis must not fetch data from the internet.
Use sample standard deviation and document data exclusions.

rubric_items.criterion: Per-station summaries and wettest station-month match independently computed fixture values.
rubric_items.check_method: Run the analysis on a fixed CSV and compare each station statistic and the selected maximum month with independently calculated expected values.

rubric_items.criterion: Missing and nonnumeric measurements are reported as invalid rows.
rubric_items.check_method: Run fixtures containing a blank and a nonnumeric millimeter value and assert both row numbers appear in validation output.

rubric_items.criterion: The methods section explains statistical choices and data limitations accurately.
rubric_items.check_method: A reviewer checks the sample-standard-deviation rationale, exclusion policy, and limitations against the assignment.

planner_response.plan_summary: Implement local CSV validation and reproducible per-station statistics, then create the chart, regression checks, and methods documentation.
evidence: Tasks cover all requested input validation, four per-station statistics, wettest station-month, comparison chart, offline behavior, fixtures, tests, and methods notes.

nodes.description: Load the local rainfall CSV and report rows missing required or numeric values.
acceptance_criteria: The parser reports the source row for blank and nonnumeric millimeter values and exits without fetching network data.

nodes.description: Calculate observation count, mean, median, and sample standard deviation per station.
acceptance_criteria: The fixed fixture reports the independently calculated count, mean, median, and ddof=1 standard deviation for every station.

nodes.description: Identify the station and month with the largest valid rainfall measurement.
acceptance_criteria: The result identifies the fixture's expected station-month pair and its millimeter value.

nodes.description: Create a labeled chart comparing station-level rainfall summaries.
acceptance_criteria: A chart artifact exists with all four station labels, a rainfall unit label, and a descriptive title.

nodes.description: Add fixture tests for statistics, wettest month, and invalid-row diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests compare all station statistics and the maximum pair with fixed expected values and assert both invalid-row numbers.

nodes.description: Document reproducible invocation, sample standard deviation, and data exclusions.
acceptance_criteria: The methods section defines sample standard deviation, states the invalid-row policy, and gives a command that runs offline.
